title: 6. National Pension System (NPS) – VERY HIGH PROBABILITY

blocks.content: The National Pension System (NPS) is a voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme designed to enable subscribers to make optimum decisions regarding their future through systematic savings.

rows: No tax benefits (Except Central Govt Employees with 3-year lock-in)

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: National Pension System (NPS) was launched in January 2004 for government employees and opened to all Indian citizens in May 2009.
Regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) under the statutory PFRDA Act, 2013.
Operates on a defined contribution framework where individual contributions are invested in equity, corporate bonds, government securities, and alternative assets.
Provides two distinct account tiers: Tier-I (non-withdrawable pension account) and Tier-II (voluntary withdrawable savings account).
Offers unique tax advantages under Section 80CCD(1B) of the Income Tax Act up to an additional limit of ₹50,000.
PFRDA regulates NPS, not RBI or SEBI — frequently targeted as a distractor option in prelims exams.
Exclusive additional tax deduction of ₹50,000 is available under Section 80CCD(1B), over and above the ₹1.5 lakh limit under Section 80C.
Maximum joining age for non-government citizens was extended from 65 to 70 years.
Tier-I is mandatory for receiving pension benefits, whereas Tier-II account requires an active Tier-I account to open.
